+# Connect Azure environments in the Defender portal - Microsoft Defender for Cloud | Microsoft Learn
+
+Important
+
+This feature is in preview. For more information, see [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/).
+
+Connect Azure subscriptions and management groups to manage cloud security plans in the Microsoft Defender portal. The connector establishes the cloud security access and permissions required for the selected Azure environment.
+
+Connecting an environment doesn't change its existing plans or billing. If cloud security plans are already enabled, they appear in the Defender portal, and the connector permissions replace the environment's existing cloud security access model. If no plans are enabled, enable them separately after the connector is active.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin, make sure you have:
+
+- An Azure commercial environment.
+
+    Note
+
+    Azure national or sovereign clouds aren't currently supported.
+- The **Global Administrator** or **Security Administrator** role in Microsoft Entra ID. Alternatively, you need the **Core security settings (Manage)** permission in [Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC)](/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-permissions-details#authorization-and-settings).
+- The **Owner** or **User Access Administrator** role on the Azure subscription or management group that you want to connect.
+
+    Note
+
+    You might need to [elevate access to manage Azure subscriptions and management groups](/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/elevate-access-global-admin?tabs=azure-portal%2Centra-audit-logs).
+
+## Prepare your tenant
+
+The first time you access **Cloud security** in the Defender portal, Defender prepares your tenant by collecting information about your Azure subscriptions, including their current coverage and enabled plans.
+
+Tenant preparation can take up to an hour. You can begin connecting environments while preparation continues.
+
+## Connect an Azure environment
+
+To connect an Azure environment:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. Go to **Cloud security** > **Overview**.
+3. Under **Manage cloud security**, select **Connect environments**.
+4. Select **Connector page**.
+5. Under **Microsoft Azure**, select **Connect**.
+6. Optionally, enter a display name for the connector.
+7. Select whether you want to connect a **Management Group** or **Subscription**.
+8. Enter the management group ID or subscription ID, depending on the environment type you selected.
+
+    If you don't enter a display name, this ID is used instead.
+9. Select **Next**.
+10. Select the capabilities that you want to enable for the environment:
+
+    - **Discovery** identifies resources and builds the cloud inventory.
+    - **Agent deployment** deploys and manages agents in the environment.
+    - **AI access** reads supported AI prompts and resources to provide AI security insights.
+    - **Agentless scanners** scan supported resources without installing an agent.
+
+    Tip
+
+    Microsoft recommends enabling all available capabilities to maintain full security coverage and avoid protection gaps.
+11. Select **Next**.
+12. Select a deployment method: **Auto-deploy** or **Manual deployment**.
+13. **Auto-deploy only:** Select **Run auto-deploy**. The deployment and validation run automatically.
+14. **Manual deployment only:**
+
+    1. Select **Copy script**.
+    2. Open Azure Cloud Shell and select **Bash**.
+    3. Paste and run the script in Cloud Shell.
+    4. After the script finishes successfully, copy the **Security Operator ID** returned by the script.
+    5. Paste the value into **Security Operator ID**.
+    6. Select **Validate**.
+15. Select **Next**.
+16. Review the connector details, then select **Activate connector**.
+17. After the connector is successfully activated, select **Done**.
+
+After a successful connection, the Azure environment appears in the Microsoft Defender portal with any existing enabled plans. If no plans are enabled, [configure cloud security plans](manage-plans-defender-portal) separately.
+
+## Edit an existing connector
+
+You can update the capabilities and permissions assigned to an existing connector.
+
+To edit an existing connector:
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. Go to **Cloud security** > **Overview**.
+3. Under **Manage cloud security**, select **Connect environments**.
+4. Select **Connector page**.
+5. Select **My connectors**.
+6. Select the Azure connector you want to update.
+7. Select **Edit connector**.
+8. Update the connector settings.
+
+    Note
+
+    If you change the connector capabilities or permissions, redeploy and validate the connector before continuing.
+9. Select **Next**.
+10. Review the connector details, then select **Activate connector**.
+11. After the connector is successfully activated, select **Done**.

+# Estimate and track cost with new Cloud security billing model in Defender portal - Microsoft Defender for Cloud | Microsoft Learn
+
+Important
+
+This feature is in preview. For more information, see [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/).
+
+Defender Workload Units (DWUs) provide a unified model for estimating Microsoft Defender for Cloud costs. Use the Cloud Security Cost Estimator before enabling protection, and use the Cloud security cost report to review actual costs over time.
+
+## Defender Workload Units
+
+A Defender Workload Unit represents cloud security usage across supported workload types. Each protected workload contributes to DWU usage according to its type and counting model.
+
+The same underlying model is used for:
+
+- Cost estimation
+- Cost reporting
+- Billing
+
+The DWU model replaces separate billing signals with one unit that can be reviewed across workloads and environments. For current pricing and workload mappings, see [Microsoft Defender for Cloud pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/defender-for-cloud/).
+
+As part of the new model:
+
+- Defender for Containers is measured by protected node instead of vCPU.
+- Defender for Key Vault, Defender for Storage, and Defender for Resource Manager use per-resource measurement instead of transactional measurement.
+- Defender for Azure SQL Databases, Defender for SQL Servers on Machines, and Defender for Open-Source Relational Databases are consolidated into one Defender for Databases plan.
+- Defender for APIs uses a unified plan instead of multiple separate plans.
+- Defender for DNS will no longer be offered as a standalone plan. Defender for Servers Plan 2 customers gain access to Defender for DNS value as part of Defender for Servers Plan 2 at no extra cost.
+
+## Estimate cloud security costs
+
+Use the Cloud Security Cost Estimator to estimate DWU usage and projected monthly costs before moving environments to the new model.
+
+1. Open the [Cloud Security Cost Estimator](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/cloud-security/cost-estimator).
+2. Sign in if prompted.
+3. Review the supported workload categories and their DWU mappings.
+4. Enter the number of resources you want to protect for one or more workloads.
+5. Review the calculated DWUs and estimated monthly cost for each workload.
+6. Review the total DWUs and estimated monthly cost.
+7. Adjust the resource quantities to compare different coverage scenarios.
+
+The estimate updates automatically when you change a workload quantity.
+
+## Track cloud security cost
+
+After you move subscriptions to DWU-based billing, use the Cloud security cost report to review costs.
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. In the navigation pane, select **Cost & usage**.
+
+The Cloud security cost page shows the total USD cost for the selected time period in the upper-right corner of the **Spending overview** chart.
+
+## Analyze cloud security costs
+
+Use **Group by** and **Add filter** at the top of the **Cost analysis** chart to review costs by:
+
+- Meter name
+- Billing subscription name
+- Product name
+
+Hover over the cost graph to review spending in USD. Use the toggle in the upper-right corner of the **Cost analysis** chart to switch between daily and cumulative spending.
+
+Note
+
+Cloud security costs can fluctuate from day to day even when there are no changes to the connected environments or their resources.

+# Manage cloud security plans in the Defender portal - Microsoft Defender for Cloud | Microsoft Learn
+
+Important
+
+This feature is in preview. For more information, see [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/).
+
+Use the Microsoft Defender portal to configure cloud security plans across connected Azure environments. You can apply plans globally to all current and future connected environments or configure plans for selected management groups and subscriptions.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you begin:
+
+- To configure plans for specific management groups or subscriptions, [connect the Azure environments](connect-azure-environments-defender-portal) that you want to manage. You don't need to connect each environment before configuring global plan enablement, which applies automatically to current and future connected environments.
+- The **Global Administrator** or **Security Administrator** role in Microsoft Entra ID. Alternatively, you need the **Core security settings (Manage)** permission in [Microsoft Defender unified role-based access control (RBAC)](/en-us/defender-xdr/custom-permissions-details#authorization-and-settings).
+- Review [changes to Defender for Cloud plan management in the Defender portal](plan-management-changes-defender-portal).
+
+Note
+
+Cloud security plan management in the Defender portal currently supports Azure commercial environments only. AWS, GCP, Azure national or sovereign clouds, Azure DevOps, GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, and Docker Hub aren't supported in this experience. GitHub is supported separately in public preview. For setup instructions, see [Create a GitHub connector](/en-us/security-exposure-management/create-github-connector).
+
+## What happens when you manage plans in the Defender portal
+
+Azure environments continue to use Azure-based plan management until one of the following actions occurs:
+
+- You migrate a specific connected environment to the Defender portal.
+- You configure global plan enablement at the tenant level. All current connected environments are migrated automatically, and future connected environments inherit the same configuration.
+
+After migration, plan configuration is managed in the Defender portal and appears as view-only in the Azure portal. Cost information is available in the Cloud security cost report.
+
+Important
+
+Resource-level plan configurations aren't preserved when plan management moves to the Defender portal. Plan coverage is configured at the management-group or subscription level and applies to the resources under that scope.
+
+## Choose how to edit and enable cloud security plans
+
+You can enable cloud security plans in either of the following ways:
+
+| Configuration | Use |
+| --- | --- |
+| Global plan enablement | Set cloud security plans globally for all connected and newly connected environments. |
+| Per-environment plan configuration | Configure security plans for selected environments and groups. |
+
+## Configure plans for selected environments
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. Go to **Cloud security**.
+3. Under **Manage cloud security**, select **Define Cloud Security plans**.
+4. Under **Per-environment plan configurations**, select **View environments**.
+5. Select **Groups** or **Environments**, depending on the scope you want to configure.
+6. When prompted, approve moving plan management for the selected environments to the Defender portal. To understand the effects of this change, see [What changes when managing cloud security plans in the Defender portal](plan-management-changes-defender-portal).
+
+    [![Screenshot showing the environment details pane with the option to review migration details.](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/selected-environment-review-migration.png)](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/selected-environment-review-migration.png#lightbox)
+7. Select **Edit plans**.
+
+    If you selected multiple environments, select **Bulk edit coverage**.
+8. Enable or disable the plans you want to apply.
+
+    [![Screenshot showing the Edit plans pane for an Azure management group in the Defender portal.](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/selected-environment-edit-plans.png)](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/selected-environment-edit-plans.png#lightbox)
+9. If prompted, choose whether to start the 30-day free trial for eligible subscriptions.
+10. Configure the available plan settings and extensions.
+
+To prevent child environments from overriding the configuration, select the lock icon.
+
+## Configure global plan enablement
+
+1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Defender portal](https://security.microsoft.com).
+2. Go to **Cloud security**.
+3. Under **Manage cloud security**, select **Define Cloud Security plans**.
+4. Under **Global plans enablement**, select **Global plans enablement page**.
+5. When prompted, approve moving cloud security plan management for current and future connected environments to the Defender portal. This is a one-time tenant-level approval that applies automatically to all existing and future connected environments.
+6. Enable or disable the cloud security plans that you want to apply.
+
+    [![Screenshot showing global security plan enablement settings, including plan selection and the Save and apply button.](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/global-plan-enablement.png)](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/global-plan-enablement.png#lightbox)
+7. If prompted, choose whether to start the 30-day free trial for eligible subscriptions.
+8. Configure the available settings and extensions for each plan.
+9. Review the changes, and then confirm the configuration.
+
+The configuration applies to all current and newly connected environments.
+
+To prevent child environments from overriding the global configuration, select the lock icon.
+
+## Cloud security trial behavior
+
+You can start a 30-day free trial for all eligible cloud security plans when you enable plans in the Defender portal.
+
+The trial requires explicit opt-in. During the trial, eligible environments receive access to all eligible cloud security plans.
+
+The trial selection applies to the scope where you enable the plans. When you start the trial at the tenant or management-group level, the selection is inherited by eligible environments under that scope, including:
+
+- Existing eligible environments.
+- Future eligible environments added under that scope.
+
+Each future eligible environment receives its own 30-day free trial when it becomes eligible.
+
+If you enable plans without starting the trial, the trial is no longer available for those environments and billing begins immediately.
+
+You can change the trial selection for a scope later. Changes apply from that point forward. A trial that already started for an environment isn't canceled, extended, or reset by a later change.
+
+After the trial ends, DWU billing begins unless all cloud security plans are disabled before the trial expires.
+
+Moving plan management from the Azure portal to the Defender portal doesn't create, extend, or reset trial eligibility. An environment that previously used its cloud security trial isn't eligible for another trial.
+
+## Plan statuses and inheritance
+
+Cloud security plan management uses the Azure management hierarchy to determine which plan configuration applies to an environment.
+
+| Status | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Unconfigured (Inherit)** | No configuration is applied directly. The environment inherits its plan setting from the nearest configured parent. |
+| **Enabled** | The plan and its extensions are enabled. An inherited configuration appears as **Enabled (Inherited)**. |
+| **Disabled** | The plan and its extensions are disabled. An inherited configuration appears as **Disabled (Inherited)**. |
+
+The following inheritance rules apply:
+
+- Settings configured at a higher scope flow down to underlying environments.
+- A plan state configured directly in the Defender portal isn't automatically replaced by another higher-level setting.
+- When **Enforce and lock** is enabled, the higher-level configuration overrides settings on child environments, including settings configured directly on those environments. Child environments can't override the enforced configuration.
+
+## Configure plan extensions
+
+You can configure the extensions associated with an enabled plan.
+
+- Enabling a plan enables its extensions by default.
+- Disabling a plan disables its extensions by default.
+- Use the settings control next to a plan to enable or disable individual extensions.
+
+## Review environment coverage
+
+Use the environments page to verify the plan coverage applied to your Azure environments and see where their security plans are managed.
+
+1. Go to **Cloud security**.
+2. Under **Manage cloud security**, select **Define Cloud Security plans**.
+3. Under **Per-environment plan configurations**, select **View environments**.
+4. Use **All**, **Groups**, or **Environments** to choose the hierarchy level you want to review.
+5. Review the plan enablement status, subscription coverage, and where security plans are managed for each environment.
+
+    [![Screenshot showing the Environments management table with plan enablement status and the portal managing each plan highlighted.](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/environment-coverage-status.png)](media/manage-plans-defender-portal/environment-coverage-status.png#lightbox)
+
+Hover over an environment's plan enablement status to view its current status. For detailed coverage information, select the environment and review the coverage across its hierarchy.

+# What changes when managing cloud security plans in the Defender portal - Microsoft Defender for Cloud | Microsoft Learn
+
+Important
+
+This feature is in preview. For more information, see [Supplemental Terms of Use for Microsoft Azure Previews](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/).
+
+When you move Defender for Cloud plan management from the Azure portal to the Microsoft Defender portal, the way that plans are billed, configured, and applied changes.
+
+Before moving an Azure environment, review the following changes:
+
+- Billing moves to the Defender Workload Unit model.
+- Plan configuration moves from resource-level settings to tenant-level, management-group, and subscription settings.
+- Some existing plans are replaced, consolidated, or measured differently.
+
+## Defender Workload Unit billing
+
+After an Azure subscription moves to Defender portal plan management, billing is based on Defender Workload Units (DWUs).
+
+Each supported protected workload maps to a defined number of DWUs. The same unit model is used for:
+
+- Cost estimation
+- Usage reporting
+- Billing
+
+For more information about estimating and reviewing DWU usage, see [Estimate and track Cloud security cost](estimate-track-costs).
+
+## Scope-based plan management
+
+The Defender portal uses a top-down plan-management model.
+
+Plans and their settings are configured at the tenant, management-group, or subscription level. Resource-level plan configuration isn't supported.
+
+When a plan is enabled for a subscription, either directly or through an inherited configuration:
+
+- All supported resources in the subscription receive protection.
+- New supported resources created in the subscription inherit protection automatically.
+- Plan coverage is applied consistently across the subscription.
+
+When a plan is disabled for a subscription, protection is removed from all supported resources in that subscription.
+
+Important
+
+Existing resource-level configurations aren't preserved when plan management moves from the Azure portal to the Defender portal. They are replaced by the configuration applied at the management-group or subscription scope.
+
+After an environment moves to Defender portal management:
+
+- Plan configuration is managed in the Defender portal.
+- Plan configuration appears as view-only in the Azure portal.
+- Billing for migrated subscriptions uses DWUs.
+- Cost becomes available in the Cloud Security Cost & usage report.
+
+## Security plan changes
+
+Some existing plans are replaced, consolidated, or measured differently when they move to the Defender portal.
+
+| Current plan | Updated plan or behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| Defender for Key Vault billed by transaction | Defender for Key Vault billed per resource |
+| Defender for Storage V1 billed by transaction | Defender for Storage V2 billed per resource |
+| Defender for Resource Manager billed by transaction | Defender for Resource Manager billed per resource |
+| Defender for Containers billed by vCPU | Defender for Containers billed by protected node |
+| Defender for Azure SQL Databases, Defender for SQL Servers on Machines, and Defender for Open-Source Relational Databases | Consolidated Defender for Databases plan |
+| Defender for DNS | Continue without DNS protection, or enable Defender for Servers Plan 2 |
+
+Most supported plans are mapped automatically to the new model.
+
+Defender for DNS isn't carried forward automatically. During migration, choose whether to:
+
+- Continue without DNS protection.
+- Enable Defender for Servers Plan 2, which includes DNS protection and might result in additional charges.
+
+Review the changes shown in the Defender portal before confirming the migration.

-# Enable preview features in the Defender portal - Microsoft Defender for Cloud | Microsoft Learn
-
-Defender for Cloud expansion to the Defender portal is in preview phase and aligns to the general preview feature guidelines and support: [Microsoft Defender XDR preview features](/en-us/defender-xdr/preview)
-
-Note
-
-Enabling preview features in Defender portal does not impact Defender for Cloud in the Azure portal, they live side by side.
-
-## Prerequisites
-
-Defender for Cloud with at least one paid plan is eligible to experience the Defender for Cloud preview capabilities in the Defender portal.
-
-Accounts must have one of the following Entra ID roles:
-
-- Global Administrator
-- Security Administrator
-
-## How to enable
-
-In the Microsoft Defender portal, navigate to **Settings** > **Microsoft Defender XDR** > **General** > **Preview features**, and select to turn on preview features.
-
-Ensure both "Microsoft Defender XDR" and "Microsoft Defender for Cloud" options are selected.
-
-## What happens after you enable preview features
-
-After you enable preview features, expect the following changes:
-
-- Preview features may take up to 24 hours to turn on.
-- Enabling preview features introduces new security recommendations in preview in the Azure portal.
-- Once preview features are enabled, find Defender for Cloud in the left menu under **Cloud security**.

Updated October 19, 2026: We have identified that this message did not reach it's intended audience. You can safely disregard this message, and we apologize any confusion this may have caused.

What and why:

Microsoft Security Copilot agents are built into the flow of work of security teams using Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Intune and Microsoft Purview. At Ignite 2025, Microsoft introduced a dozen new agents across these products, bringing agentic defense across workflows to enable autonomous and proactive protection.

Rollout schedule:

N/A

Impact on your organization:

Who is affected:

  • Organizations with Microsoft 365 E5 or E7

Platforms/Services:

  • Defender
  • Entra
  • Intune
  • Purview
  • Security Copilot portal

What will happen:

  • Security Copilot will be automatically included with Microsoft 365 E5/E7 (no separate purchase required).
  • Your tenant will receive 400 Security Compute Units (SCUs) per month per 1,000 licensed users, up to 10,000 SCUs per month.
  • Core agentic security experiences will be available across Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, and the Security Copilot portal.
  • Developer tools and APIs will be available to build custom agents and integrations.
  • Existing security, compliance, and access policies continue to apply.

Additional capabilities outside the included entitlement may incur extra charges, including:

  • Microsoft Sentinel data lake compute or storage.
  • Non-agentic Data Security Investigations in Purview.
  • Azure Logic Apps usage with Security Copilot.
  • Third-party agents purchased via Microsoft Security Store.

Action required / Recommendations:

No action is required to enable this feature.

We recommend:

  • Reviewing new agentic scenarios and capabilities in the Security Copilot Adoption Hub.
  • Reviewing the documentation for details on what’s included.
  • Requesting assistance from a Microsoft 365 FastTrack specialist to unlock the full value of Security Copilot.
  • Exploring Microsoft and partner-published agents in Microsoft Security Store, also accessible within Microsoft Defender and Entra.

If you would like to opt out of this entitlement, please contact support.
